## Summary

I reconstructed a whole-building lightweight BIM (**candidate_04**, delivered via `finish_bim`) from the two floor plans (1f_view.png, 2f_view.png) and four elevations (North/South/East/West_view.png).

**Building**: 15.0m × 8.0m footprint, 2 storeys (F1 height 3.0m, F2 height 3.6m, total 6.6m, matching all four elevations exactly).

**Layout** (same pattern both floors, independently verified from each plan): a full-width central corridor separates a front row of rooms from a back row. F1 has 3 rooms per row (office/office/office on the front row; lounge/office/meeting on the back row, matching sofa, L-desk and round-table furniture respectively), with a main west entrance and a secondary south door into the lounge. F2 has 2 large meeting rooms (front row, oval tables) and 4 offices (back row, desk+monitor), with corridor windows on east/west instead of a ground door. All partitions, 14 spaces and 29 openings (14 doors, 15 windows) were checked via `check_source_space_relation` (8 sampled same/separate pairs, all consistent) and inspected against the source overlays.

**Heights**: Window heights for both floors were measured from North_view.png's vertical dimension chain (800/1800/1000/400/1600/1000mm) and applied via recorded, adopted claims: F1 windows z=[1.0,2.6]m, F2 windows z=[4.0,5.8]m (confirmed against the value already used). Door heights (main entrance, south room door, all interior corridor doors) remain an explicit 2.1m **assumption** — no elevation carried a precise mm label for doors, only an approximate visual span consistent with ~2.0–2.1m.

**Room uses**: all 14 spaces assigned an inferred role (office/corridor/lounge-breakroom/conference-meeting) with furniture-based evidence recorded via `set_space_role`.

**Unresolved/limitations honestly carried in the BIM**:
- Interior partition wall thickness not modeled (centerlines only, consistent with the lightweight plan_partition scope).
- Interior corridor/door heights are assumed, not measured.
- Pixel-to-world calibration was self-supplied from each drawing's own dimension lines, not independently cross-verified (one minor 0.4% cross-axis calibration disagreement noted on F2, within acceptable tolerance for this scale).
- No vertical circulation (stairs) was shown in either plan, so none was invented; the two floors are stacked without an explicit connecting element.
